painting-mss.name: drawing
painting-mss.title: drawing
painting-mss.reason: This is a traditional-style watercolor drawing depicting the Mandan Buffalo Dance, showing dancers in buffalo robes and painted regalia performing before earth-lodge village dwellings, a documented Mandan ceremony from their own homeland — a clear ethnographic/documentary depiction consistent with the claimed people.

painting-mss.name: board, reproduction, working, Sha-ko-ka
painting-mss.title: board, reproduction, working, Sha-ko-ka
painting-mss.reason: This is a framed reproduction print of George Catlin's painting "Sha-ko-ka, The Mint," a documentary portrait of a Mandan girl in traditional dress with quilled/beaded garment, shell ornaments and hairpipe necklaces, reproduced by the Smithsonian. It directly depicts a Mandan subject in traditional attire, fitting the claimed ethnicity.

painting-mss.name: drawing
painting-mss.title: drawing
painting-mss.reason: This depicts the Okipa ceremony figure Oke-hee-de (Foolish One) being taunted by women, a well-documented Mandan ritual scene drawn by a Mandan artist (likely Four Bears/Mato-Tope style tradition) depicting their own Okipa rite.

painting-mss.name: drawing
painting-mss.title: drawing
painting-mss.reason: This is a watercolor drawing depicting Mandan women and children in a ceremonial scene (related to the Okipa/O-kee-pa ceremony with the figure O-ke-hee-de), showing traditional dress, dentalium/shell necklaces, and fringed hide garments — a documentary-style depiction of Mandan ceremonial life, likely from the known 19th-century Mandan ceremony illustration series.

painting-mss.name: drawing
painting-mss.title: drawing
painting-mss.reason: This is a watercolor depicting the Mandan Okipa ceremony, showing O-ke-hee-de (the Evil Spirit) pursuing Buffalo dancers before an audience of Mandan onlookers — a documented Mandan ritual, likely after George Catlin's work. It directly illustrates Mandan ceremonial practice and dress.

painting-mss.name: drawing
painting-mss.title: drawing
painting-mss.reason: This is George Catlin's watercolor depicting the Mandan village with earth lodges, the Big Canoe/Ark ceremonial structure, medicine pole flags, and buffalo skulls associated with the O-kee-pa ceremony — a documentary ethnographic drawing of actual Mandan ceremonial architecture and practice, made by a European-American artist from firsthand observation.

household.name: Paddel, paddle
household.title: Paddel, paddle
household.reason: A wooden canoe paddle with painted red decorative motifs, collected at Fort Berthold Indian Agency, North Dakota — a Mandan-associated location — and a plausible everyday/household item used by this people.

garment.name: shoe, footwear
garment.title: shoe, footwear
garment.reason: A beaded hide moccasin, with the museum's note explicitly reading "Chief Yonktonau... Mandan" tying it to Mandan Plains footwear; beadwork and hide are typical Plains moccasin construction.
